input.question: If Q_pi(lambda; kappa) denotes the polynomial family arising from the low-rank closure relations and P_pi(lambda, kappa) denotes the family from the high-rank closure relations, does the identity Q_pi(lambda; kappa) = P_pi(lambda, kappa - lambda + pi) hold for every admissible lambda, kappa, and pi?

original_question: If Q_pi(lambda; kappa) denotes the polynomial family arising from the low-rank closure relations and P_pi(lambda, kappa) denotes the family from the high-rank closure relations, does the identity Q_pi(lambda; kappa) = P_pi(lambda, kappa - lambda + pi) hold for every admissible lambda, kappa, and pi?

original_paper.title: Concept of a veritable osp(1|2) super-triangle sum rule with 6-j^S symbols from intrinsic operator techniques: an open problem

rewritten_question: Let S_κ(c0, d0) be the iterated osp(1|2) tensor operators under study, and let P_π(λ, μ) be the polynomial family defined by the high-rank closure relation for the component [S_λ × S_μ]_{λ+μ−π}. Let Q_π(λ; κ) be the polynomial family defined by the low-rank closure relation for the component [S_λ × S_κ]_{κ−λ+π}. Here λ and κ are nonnegative integral or half-integral ranks, and π ranges over the admissible half-integer steps for which the corresponding closure relations exist: for P_π one has 0 ≤ π ≤ min(λ, μ), and for Q_π, after assuming κ ≥ λ, one has 0 ≤ π ≤ λ − 1/2. Is the low-rank family always obtained from the high-rank family by the shift of the second argument κ ↦ κ − λ + π, so that for every admissible triple one has Q_π(λ; κ) = P_π(λ, κ − λ + π)?

resolution.status_reason: The primary paper states this identity as Conjecture 2 and later describes the functional relation between the P and Q polynomial families as part of the open work still remaining. In a bounded later-literature search, the exact OpenAlex record for the paper shows zero citations, and targeted OpenAlex and Crossref searches did not surface a later academic paper explicitly proving or superseding this conjectured identity.

Conjecture 2: The relation between Qπ and Pπ polynomials is given by Qπ(λ; κ) = Pπ(λ, κ − λ + π).

Section 13, a very important one, sets precisely all the polynomial definitions and conditions, which seem necessary for achieving the ultimate identification process over a lot of binomials. However, in addition with a paradoxical remark about osp(1|2) (may be false), we give up finding an analytical solution to our problem, thus declared ‘open’.

Whatsoever the final solution, the yet simple hypothesis of a triangle sum rule for osp(1|2) involves a lot of problems, including rigorous proof of weak conjectures, like the fact that x coefficients are integral numbers (see sect. 8) and functional relations between polynomials Pω and Qω (see sect. 10). That displays a rather vast and promising work remaining to achieve.
